newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil firms on India import.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil firms on India import.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps firmed late afternoon on Monday following a higher-than-expected award by India and expectations of continued physical support from a local trader.
"The market took off this afternoon after news of the IOC (Indian Oil Corp) award," one trader said. "People are also expecting Hin Leong's buying to continue."
The April gas oil was last quoted at $27.00/$27.15 up from Friday's $26.65/$26.75. Brokers said the market traded in the afternoon after a slow start at $27.00 and $27.15.
They said the April/May time spread widened to value at around $1.00 per barrel compared to Friday's traded level of 85 cents.

Traders said local trader Hin Leong's recent effort to support the market received a timely boost from the IOC award as the bigger award was expected to absorb some of the expected arbitrage cargoes originally designated to East Asia.
IOC awarded a total of 870,000 tonnes of diesel for May arrival, well above even the most bullish prediction of around 800,000-tonnes made on Friday.
As a result of the IOC award, many felt that Hin Leong might be encouraged to bid for more cargoes on the Singapore physical market.
Hin Leong has bought more than four million barrels of gas oil since early March, thereby raising the price by over $3.00 per barrel.

However, in the fuel oil market similar attempts to support prices were proving more difficult due to large stocks in Singapore on top of an expected 250,000-tonne of arbitrage cargoes due in the region after mid-April.
April fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $98.00/$99.00 per tonne, down from Friday's $99.50/100.50 per tonne, brokers said.
In the physical market, Hin Leong bought a 20,000-tonne cargo late on Friday at $102.50 per tonne free-on-board Singapore, compared to the $104.00 traded on Thursday.
